entries.name: A-Frame
entries.use_for: Build VR/AR experiences for the web with HTML-like markup on top of three.js.
entries.why: Easiest entry to WebXR; declarative entity-component system with many community components.

entries.name: Babylon.js
entries.use_for: Full 3D rendering and game engine for the web, with physics, XR and an inspector.
entries.why: Batteries-included engine backed by Microsoft, strong WebGPU support and tooling (Playground, Inspector).

entries.name: drei
entries.use_for: Ready-made helpers (controls, loaders, text, environments) for React Three Fiber.
entries.why: Saves writing common R3F building blocks by hand; maintained by the R3F team.

entries.name: Fabric.js
entries.use_for: Interactive object model on canvas: select, transform, serialize, SVG import/export
entries.why: Classic choice for in-browser image and design editors

entries.name: Filament
entries.use_for: Real-time physically based rendering engine for Android, iOS, desktop and WebGL.
entries.why: Google-maintained PBR renderer that is small enough for mobile apps.

entries.name: GPU.js
entries.use_for: Run general-purpose compute kernels on the GPU from JavaScript
entries.why: Transpiles plain JS functions to WebGL/WebGL2 shaders with CPU fallback; the standard way to do GPGPU in browser and Node.

entries.name: Konva
entries.use_for: 2D canvas scene graph with shapes, events and drag-and-drop; React and Vue bindings
entries.why: Most popular 2D canvas framework for interactive editors and diagrams

entries.name: luma.gl
entries.use_for: High-performance WebGL2/WebGPU rendering toolkit for GPU-heavy visualization
entries.why: The GPU layer under deck.gl (vis.gl / OpenJS); WebGPU-ready

license_verified.note: MIT per LICENSE (GitHub cannot classify due to attribution notes)

entries.name: model-viewer
entries.use_for: Drop a 3D glTF model with AR and camera controls into any page via a web component
entries.why: Google's easy path to embedding 3D/AR on the web without writing three.js code

entries.name: PixiJS
entries.use_for: Fast 2D rendering on WebGL/WebGPU for interactive graphics and games.
entries.why: The leading 2D renderer for the web; great when you need many sprites with high performance.

entries.name: PlayCanvas Engine
entries.use_for: Lightweight web graphics runtime for 3D apps and games, including Gaussian splats.
entries.why: Fast, small engine with WebGPU and WebXR support; powers the PlayCanvas editor.

entries.name: postprocessing
entries.use_for: Bloom, SSAO, depth of field and other post effects for three.js
entries.why: Standard post-processing library for three.js, faster than the built-in EffectComposer; powers react-postprocessing

entries.name: React Three Fiber
entries.use_for: Build three.js scenes declaratively as React components.
entries.why: The default way to use three.js in React apps; pairs with drei and the wider pmndrs ecosystem.

entries.name: regl
entries.use_for: Functional, stateless WebGL wrapper for custom rendering pipelines
entries.why: Lean, battle-tested WebGL abstraction used in data-viz and research

entries.name: three-mesh-bvh
entries.use_for: Fast raycasting, collision and spatial queries on three.js meshes
entries.why: Go-to BVH acceleration for three.js; used by drei, path tracers and many editors

entries.name: three.js
entries.use_for: Render 3D scenes in the browser with WebGL or WebGPU.
entries.why: The standard 3D library for the web, with the largest ecosystem of examples, loaders and add-ons.

entries.name: Threlte
entries.use_for: Build three.js scenes declaratively in Svelte.
entries.why: The Svelte counterpart to React Three Fiber, with physics and helper packages.

entries.name: TresJS
entries.use_for: Build three.js scenes declaratively with Vue components.
entries.why: The Vue counterpart to React Three Fiber, with a Nuxt module and helper packages.

entries.name: Two.js
entries.use_for: Renderer-agnostic 2D drawing API that targets SVG, Canvas or WebGL
entries.why: Simple 2D drawing with one API across three renderers

entries.name: TypeGPU
entries.use_for: Write type-safe WebGPU code and shaders in TypeScript.
entries.why: Removes much of WebGPU boilerplate with strong type inference; maintained by Software Mansion.

entries.name: wgpu
entries.use_for: Cross-platform, safe Rust graphics API based on WebGPU, running on Vulkan, Metal, DX12 and the web.
entries.why: Foundation of most Rust graphics (Bevy, Firefox WebGPU); one API across native and browser.
